title: Austin vs Nashville: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Austin for BBQ, genre-diverse live music, and weird sprawling energy. Nashville for walkable honky tonk nightlife, country music depth, and bachelorette-friendly Broadway.

categories.name: BBQ & Food
categories.summary: Franklin Barbecue is a world-class pilgrimage. Nashville's hot chicken is excellent but BBQ isn't its strength.

categories.name: Live Music
categories.summary: Austin has 250+ venues across every genre. Nashville wins for country music specifically.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Nashville runs 10-15% cheaper overall, with free Broadway bar entry.

categories.name: Walkability
categories.summary: Broadway is walkable. Austin requires rideshares beyond 6th Street.

categories.name: Nightlife
categories.summary: Nashville's Broadway is concentrated and cover-free. Austin's Rainey Street is more eclectic.

categories.name: Bachelorette/Bachelor
categories.summary: Nashville is America's undisputed bachelorette capital.

categories.name: Outdoor Activities
categories.summary: Barton Springs, Zilker Park, Hill Country, Enchanted Rock — Austin wins outdoors.

categories.name: Weather
categories.summary: Nashville has 4 seasons. Austin summers hit 100°F+ and are brutal.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Hill Country, San Antonio, Enchanted Rock offer more diversity than Nashville's options.

categories.name: Country Music
categories.summary: Grand Ole Opry, Ryman Auditorium, Music Row — Nashville is unmatched for country.

faq.question: Is Austin or Nashville better for live music?
faq.answer: Austin wins for genre diversity (250+ venues, every genre). Nashville wins for country music specifically — Grand Ole Opry, Ryman, Music Row.

faq.question: Which has better BBQ?
faq.answer: Austin decisively. Franklin Barbecue is world-class. Nashville's hot chicken is excellent but BBQ isn't the focus.

faq.question: Which is cheaper?
faq.answer: Nashville is 10-15% cheaper overall. Budget $70-100/day Nashville vs $80-120/day Austin. Both spike during major events.
